messages:
maria: Heads up — after the FP4 calibration change rolled to canary yesterday we started seeing lower throughput on long-seq chat workloads. Tokens/sec down ~18% on p3s, memory a bit spikier. Anyone else see this?
kenji: saw alerts. p99 latency jumped on a few routes. Not universal but repeats on sessions with >1024 prefix.
odds: which canary? how many hosts?
maria: canary tag: fp4-calib-v3, ~10% of traffic in prod, GPU type: a100s + some p3s in dedicated lab. I triggered tracing for a sample trace: nvprof+timing.
dana: paste the profile snippet?
maria: ```
GPU: a100 80GB
Batch size distribution: 1:58%, 2-4:30%, 8+:12%
Observed: kernel switch hotspots at kv-cache lookup + attn matmul for seq>512
NVTX: matmul_fp4_kernel_v2  45% of time (was 28% pre-roll)
CUDA mem allocated spiked by ~12% during long sessions
Tokens/sec (avg) pre: 420, post: 345
P99 latency pre: 320ms, post: 410ms
```
oleg: interesting — kernel selection seems to prefer the new fp4 matmul for certain shapes but it looks slower for our long sequence case. Could be quantization-layout alignment, or extra unpacking cost.
kenji: I compared kernel timings on isolated microbench: fp4_matmul_v2 is faster at short seq and small batch, slower once seq*hidden crosses threshold due to extra gather/unpack loop. Might be amortization.
maria: also saw KV cache fragmentation: cache block reuse dropped ~20% for sessions >1024, causing extra re-materialization. suspect padding/runtime layout changed during calibration.
dana: can you share the sampling trace id? I can run the memprof hooks and check allocator fragmentation.
maria: trace: trace-1792001023-5. I uploaded nvprof + allocation trace to /tmp/calist/trace-1792001023.tar.gz
jai: quick hypothesis: calibration changed quant params per-head leading to per-layer fallback codepath for some tensors that forces extra memcpy into float32 for some attention kernels. That explains both CPU memcpy and memory spike.
kenji: confirmed with lightweight run: set ENV FP4_FORCE_OLD_LAYOUT=1 and perf returns to baseline on same sample (tokens/sec 418).
odds: so layout change is likely the culprit. Why did calibration flip layout for those layers?
maria: the calibrator now picks per-channel scale vs per-tensor in v3 to improve quality, but we didn't gate the kernel selection to require matching packed layout. Kernel selection assumed per-tensor packing.
oleg: good catch. Options: (A) revert calibrator change on canary; (B) make kernel selection aware of per-channel pack and fallback to legacy matmul for long sequence; (C) add a fast path to pack on the fly (also costs memcpy).
dana: short-term: revert to v2 calibrator for canary and start incident rollback. Long-term: we should add a telemetry counter that emits ``kernel_pack_mismatch`` count and sample stack for occurrences.
maria: agreed. I'll open rollback PR and push config to flip canary back. Also adding a metric: runtime.kernel_pack_mismatch (tag: model, layer, seq_bucket).
kenji: I'll work on kernel selector: if pack_style != expected_pack and seq_len>512 prefer legacy matmul kernel. Add unit test.
jai: we should also add a microbench step to CI that validates new calibration doesn't change packing layout for any layer in our supported models (gpt2/gpt-j/llama variants).
oleg: creating follow-up ticket: PERF-4BIT-845 "FP4 calibrator -> kernel packing mismatch causing throughput regressions". Assign to kenji + dana.
sre-bot: deploy rollback started for canary group fp4-calib-v3 -> fp4-calib-v2 (10 hosts). Estimated 6m.
maria: after rollback started, observed partial recovery in metrics on canary cluster. tokens/sec climbed back to ~410 within 8 min. memory spike subsided.
dana: next steps: 1) rollback fully 2) deploy metric patch 3) add CI microbench 4) kernel selector guard 5) re-run calibration in staging with explicit packing flag.
kenji: will PR guard and tests by EOD. dana and maria can push metric changes. jai please add CI microbench item.
maria: thanks all. I'll update the incident board and ping infra for a longer soak in staging with real long-session traffic after we validate. :thumbsup:
